# PR: The arrival moment — greet share-link recipients and convert them (backlog 007)

**Risk tier (builder's guess): HIGH** — per 007.md's own pre-classification and NORTH_STAR.md's
risk map ("anything user-facing beyond copy/styling" → HIGH → full explainer + quiz before
merge). This adds a new, always-on-first-view UI surface to the planner's primary conversion
path. Git is unavailable in this environment (task constraint: no git operations, read-only bash
mount), so there is no branch or commit — this file is the PR, reviewable at the working-tree
paths cited below.

## Goal
NORTH_STAR's north-star metric is the funnel `share_link_opened → plan_created`. Spec 005
(shipped earlier today) fixed the funnel's first step — the share mechanisms now reliably carry a
URL. This item is the funnel's **second** step: `share_link_opened` already fires the moment a
recipient's browser decodes a shared URL (planner.js:3416-3422), but until now that decode was
silent — the recipient landed straight in a fully-prefilled planner with no acknowledgment that
someone sent them this, no framing, no next action. 007.md's evidence: "Funnel step 2 conversion
is structurally left to chance." Goal: give that moment an explicit, honest, dismissible greeting
with one path forward, so the second half of the funnel has a designed moment instead of an
accident.

## Intuition
The instinct going in was that this would require a mode-aware placement (a banner for the
"report" screen, a different one for the "conversation" screen) or a "claim this plan" affordance.
Investigation killed both ideas. `mode` (planner.js:3429) depends only on whether *this browser*
already has a saved plan in `localStorage` — never on the shared URL — so for the actual target
user (a fresh browser opening a friend's link), `mode` is `'convo'` for the entire session, and a
pre-existing fast-forward effect (planner.js:3505-3515) advances `step` straight to `'bloom'`
within one render, because `answers` was already seeded from the decoded share data before that
effect's guard conditions are even checked. By the time a human could see the banner, the full
prefilled plan is already rendered directly underneath it. That collapses two apparent design
problems into non-problems: the banner only needs one render location (the `gp-app` root, sibling
to `<main>`), and the CTA has nothing to navigate to — it can only mean "get out of the way," so
it does exactly that, sharing its handler with the dismiss control.

The other half of the intuition: this item's job was narrower than it first sounds. `plan_created`
already fires automatically for a share-link recipient the moment their prefilled plan's pools
finish loading (the pre-existing persist effect, planner.js:1615-1659) — no click required beyond
having arrived. Nothing in this change touches that. The task was purely to acknowledge the
arrival, not to cause the conversion that was already wired.

## What changed, walking the diff in reading order

### 1. `planner.js` — new `ArrivalBanner` component (planner.js:3320-3337), right after `PlannerHeader`
```js
function ArrivalBanner(props) {
  var t = props.t;
  // CTA and dismiss both close the banner: shared plans fast-forward straight
  // to the bloom step, so the recipient's prefilled plan is already rendered
  // underneath -- "adopting" it just means clearing this banner out of the way.
  return e('div', { className: 'gp-arrival-banner gp-animate-in' },
    e('p', { className: 'gp-arrival-text' }, t('arrivalBannerText')),
    e('div', { className: 'gp-arrival-actions' },
      e('button', { type: 'button', className: 'gp-cta gp-arrival-cta', onClick: props.onDismiss },
        t('arrivalBannerCta')),
      e('button', { type: 'button', className: 'gp-arrival-dismiss', onClick: props.onDismiss,
        'aria-label': t('arrivalBannerDismiss') }, '✕')
    )
  );
}
```
Both buttons call the identical `onDismiss` prop — see "Design decision" below for why that's
deliberate, not an oversight.

### 2. `planner.js` — dismissal state (planner.js:3465-3466), next to the existing `sharedIntroState`
```js
var arrivalDismissedState = useState(false);
var arrivalDismissed = arrivalDismissedState[0], setArrivalDismissed = arrivalDismissedState[1];
```
Plain session state, no `localStorage` — matches the spec's explicit instruction and the
already-established idiom `sharedIntroState` (planner.js:3459-3460) uses for the same class of
problem (an older, non-dismissible inline "Someone shared their garden" line).

### 3. `planner.js` — `restart()` gains one line (planner.js:3480)
```js
setShowSharedIntro(false);
setArrivalDismissed(true);   // new
```
Not named explicitly in the spec's four exclusion scenarios, but required: `sharedPlan` is a
`useMemo` computed once at mount from a `urlParams` memo with an **empty** dependency array
(planner.js:3405) — it never recomputes, even though `restart()` strips the share params from the
visible URL. Without this line, a user who explicitly clicks "Start Fresh" (reachable in one
click for every share-link recipient, since `canRestart` is true at `step === 'bloom'`,
planner.js:4089) would keep seeing "Someone sent you this garden" after wiping their plan.

### 4. `planner.js` — compute and render the banner (planner.js:4091-4106)
```js
var showArrivalBanner = !!sharedPlan && !arrivalDismissed && !(mode === 'report' && savedPlan);

return e('div', { className: 'gp-app' },
  e(PlannerHeader, { ... }),
  showArrivalBanner ? e(ArrivalBanner, { t: t, onDismiss: function () { setArrivalDismissed(true); } }) : null,
  e('main', { ... }, ...)
);
```
The third term, `!(mode === 'report' && savedPlan)`, is not literally spelled out in the spec's
four named exclusions ("normal visits, presets, `?fresh=1`, returning users loading their own
saved plan") but is required by the last one: the report branch (planner.js:3673, `if (mode ===
'report' && savedPlan)`) renders the recipient's **own** saved plan and never reads `sharedPlan`
at all, so without this term a returning user who also opens a friend's link would see the
banner's "it's already set up below" framing over the wrong plan.

### 5. `translations.js` — three new keys, both languages, immediately after `checkoutNote`
```js
// en.planner, translations.js:204-206 (checkoutNote is 203, riskEdit is now 207)
arrivalBannerText: "Someone sent you this garden — it's already set up and ready to grow.",
arrivalBannerCta: "Make it mine",
arrivalBannerDismiss: "Close",

// ko.planner, translations.js:678-680 (checkoutNote is 677, riskEdit is now 681)
arrivalBannerText: "누군가 이 정원을 보냈어요 — 이미 준비가 끝나서 바로 자랄 수 있어요.",
arrivalBannerCta: "내 것으로 만들기",
arrivalBannerDismiss: "닫기",
```
Placed per the anchor rule (immediately after `checkoutNote`, not at the end of the block) to
avoid colliding with 005's keys, which live at the end of each block — verified `sharePromptHeadline`
(005's key) is untouched and `en.planner`/`ko.planner` have equal key counts (292 each) after
this edit.

### 6. `planner-styles.css` — new rules (lines 88-133) between `.gp-main` and `.gp-tagline`
```css
.gp-arrival-banner {
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: var(--space-16);
  max-width: 760px; margin: 0 auto var(--space-16);
  padding: var(--space-14) var(--space-20);
  border-radius: var(--neuro-radius-md); background: var(--color-surface);
  box-shadow: var(--neuro-shadow-flat);
}
.gp-arrival-text { flex: 1; min-width: 0; margin: 0; font-size: var(--font-size-sm);
  font-weight: var(--font-weight-medium); color: var(--color-text); line-height: var(--line-height-normal); }
.gp-arrival-actions { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-8); flex-shrink: 0; }
.gp-arrival-cta { white-space: nowrap; }
.gp-arrival-dismiss { width: 32px; height: 32px; border: none; border-radius: var(--neuro-radius-sm);
  background: var(--color-background); color: var(--color-text-secondary);
  font-size: var(--font-size-base); font-family: var(--font-family-base); cursor: pointer;
  display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; box-shadow: var(--neuro-shadow-subtle);
  transition: box-shadow var(--duration-normal) var(--ease-standard), transform var(--duration-normal) var(--ease-standard); }
.gp-arrival-dismiss:hover { box-shadow: var(--neuro-shadow-flat); }
.gp-arrival-dismiss:active { box-shadow: var(--neuro-shadow-pressed); transform: translateY(1px); }
.gp-arrival-dismiss:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-primary); outline-offset: 2px; }
@media (max-width: 480px) {
  .gp-arrival-banner { flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-start; gap: var(--space-12); }
}
```
`.gp-arrival-text` deliberately mirrors 005's `.gp-share-prompt-text` (same four properties) for
visual consistency between the two banner-like surfaces. `.gp-arrival-dismiss` mirrors the
pre-existing `.gp-waitlist-close` pattern (planner-styles.css:2383-2405) almost line-for-line —
same size, same tokens, same hover/active/focus-visible states. Every value is a token
(`var(--...)`); no hardcoded colors, no glow shadows, no bounce easings. The CTA reuses `.gp-cta`
verbatim (no new button visuals); the banner's entrance reuses the existing `.gp-animate-in`
class rather than new keyframes.

### 7. `planner-styles.css` — one line added to the existing reduced-motion list (line 1708)
```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  ...
  .gp-my-garden-btn,
  .gp-arrival-dismiss,   /* new */
  .gp-primary-cta { transition: none; }
}
```
`.gp-cta` (used by the CTA button) and `.gp-animate-in` (used by the banner's entrance) were
**already** in this file's shared reduced-motion coverage before this change — only the one
genuinely new interactive element, the dismiss icon button, needed a line added.

## Design decision: the CTA and the dismiss button do the same thing
Covered in depth in `007-notes.md`. Short version: the spec asks for "a single CTA that moves
them into/along their prefilled plan," but the territory investigation showed a fresh recipient
is *already* on their fully-rendered, prefilled plan by the time the banner is visible — there is
no separate screen to move them to. Inventing one (a scroll target, a fabricated "claimed" flag)
would add real complexity and risk for a feature the spec explicitly asked to keep to a single
CTA. Both buttons dismiss; only the label differs — the primary button carries the adoption
framing ("Make it mine"), the small ✕ is the neutral escape hatch, matching this codebase's own
established waitlist-modal convention of pairing a labeled primary action with an unlabeled close
icon.

## Deviations from spec
- **One exclusion term beyond the four scenarios named verbatim** in 007.md (`!(mode === 'report'
  && savedPlan)`, planner.js:4095) — required so the banner never renders over a returning user's
  own report when that same user also happens to have opened someone else's share link. Detailed
  reasoning and the exact code path in `007-notes.md`.
- **`restart()` was touched** (one line) even though 007.md's OUT-of-scope list doesn't mention
  it — necessary because `sharedPlan` never recomputes after mount, so without this the banner
  would survive an explicit "Start Fresh" click. Reuses the identical pattern already established
  by `setShowSharedIntro(false)` in the same function.
- **A known, narrow gap was left unfixed and documented rather than patched**: if a returning
  user (own saved plan) opens a friend's link and then clicks "Tend"/"Edit" on their own report,
  the banner can reappear over their own editing session, because `sharedPlan` stays truthy and
  `arrivalDismissed` may still be `false`. Three conditions have to stack for this to trigger; the
  fix would require touching `onTend`/`onEdit` inside the `GardenReport` render block, outside
  this change's natural surface. Full reasoning in `007-notes.md`.
- Everything else — `encodePlanToUrl`/`decodePlanFromUrl`, router/URL semantics, analytics events
  and their firing conditions, the existing inline `sharedPlanIntro` paragraph, waitlist/checkout
  panel — untouched, as OUT of scope in 007.md.

## Verification performed
`cd defi-garden-neumorphic && node test_planner.js && node test_protocol_parsing.js && node
test_qualifier_fix.js` — all three exit 0, verified both via the `&&` chain and individually
re-run: `test_planner.js` 190/190 assertions, zero failures. `node -e
"require('./translations.js')"` loads cleanly; directly enumerated `en.planner`/`ko.planner` and
confirmed the three new keys resolve to the intended EN/KO copy in both, and that 005's
`sharePromptHeadline` key is untouched. `node -e "require('./planner.js')"` loads cleanly (36 API
keys, unchanged surface) — proves no syntax error anywhere in the file, since a `SyntaxError`
would have failed this and `test_planner.js` both. Brace-balance check on `planner-styles.css`
(577 open / 577 close). Grep-verified all five new `gp-arrival-*` selectors present exactly once,
no duplicate translation keys.

No new test file was written — this change adds no new pure/testable helper to the
`module.exports` surface (matches 004/005's precedent); it's React markup and `useState`/`useMemo`
wiring that the plain-Node harness doesn't exercise. **Not independently browser/screenshot-
verified** — no browser automation was available or appropriate in this environment (read-only,
isolated bash mount; task's own environment facts exclude `npm test`/`test_smoke.js`/Playwright).
See the final summary for exact URLs and scenarios for human visual spot-check.
